_doc: GENERATED by tools/compare_norris_1844_readings.py --build. A COMPARISON, not a reading and not an import: it holds both transcriptions of every entry the two readings disagree about, and prefers neither. Hand-edit and --check says so.
what: Norris's General Directory of Chicago for 1844, read twice: once by T-0566 (PR #704) off the Internet Archive scan generaldirectory19norr, and once by Kim Torp for genealogytrails.com, published 2002, from a different copy. Two hands, one printed book. Every disagreement below is a line one of them read differently, and those are the lines hardest to read.

archive.label: archive
archive.how: archive.org's OCR of the University of Illinois scan of the 1903 Bohan republication, committed untidied — 'Win.' for 'Wm.', 'VV.' for 'W.'

genealogytrails.label: genealogytrails
genealogytrails.how: a human transcription typed from the printed page; the transcriber states she kept spellings 'as is', added the occasional comma for readability, and marked what she could not read with (sic) or (?)

data/research/genealogytrails/text/1844d.1-24: the page title, Kim Torp's transcriber's note, and Norris's own Remarks
data/research/genealogytrails/text/1844d.1189-1194: the site navigation and the copyright line

data/research/genealogytrails/text/1844d.1-11: the page title, the transcriber's note, and Norris's Remarks repeated
data/research/genealogytrails/text/1844d.847-853: the word 'Addenda' and Norris's prose introducing it
data/research/genealogytrails/text/1844d.974-976: the site navigation and the copyright line

genealogytrails.band_headings_skipped: all-caps surname-band headings Kim Torp set between the entries, e.g. 'MOODY-NICHOLS'

method.normalisation: lowercase; & written out as and; every character outside a-z 0-9 and space dropped; runs of space collapsed. Nothing is corrected — the comparison is on the two strings as they stand.
method.matching: greedy one-to-one on the difflib SequenceMatcher ratio of the normalised strings. Pass 1 blocks on the first three letters of the leading token; pass 2 sweeps what is left against everything still unmatched, which is what recovers an entry whose first letter the OCR lost.
method.wrapped_lines: a genealogytrails line that does not begin with a capital letter is the wrapped tail of the entry above and is joined back on; five lines in this cache, all of them the bare word 'sts'
method.unambiguous_name_agreement: pass 3: where exactly one entry is left unmatched on each side sharing its first three normalised tokens, they are paired whatever the ratio — the archive OCR has swallowed the rest of the line into a ditto mark. Uniqueness on both sides is required, so two men of one name are never joined.

bands.unmatched: ratio < 0.62 against every candidate — stated as present in one reading only, never as an error in the other

method.internal_near_duplicates: CANDIDATES, reported and never removed: two entries of one reading sharing their first three normalised tokens at a ratio at or above the match threshold. A doubled band in a transcription shows up here, and the two copies of it need not agree. Two different firms of one name show up here too — Johnson, J. & A. the grocers and Johnson, J. & Co. the barbers are in both readings and are not a duplicate of anything.
method.preference: NONE. Where the two differ, both stand. This file is the record of the disagreement; it corrects nothing and deletes nothing.
